top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) rest on a genuine physics idea, the magic wavelength at which the differential light shift cancels, so many atoms can be interrogated without the trap spoiling the transition. Ye's group then brought collisional, spin-orbit and many-body effects under quantitative control and reached about 1e-18. Independent laboratories reproduce this and agree in clock-to-clock ratio comparisons, theory and experiment agree on the shifts, and the two-name allocation is the cleanest on the slate, with separable concept and realisation roles. The citation must rest on the lattice concept and its realisation, stay distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and not depend on the redefinition of the second. Twisted bilayer graphene (P002) is the more striking new matter but is about eight years old, has an unsettled pairing mechanism and an exposed credit boundary (Cao, the Dean group, earlier twisted-bilayer theory). P003 has the weakest allocation consensus and overlaps the 2016 topological prize. Any award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Possible appearance of a connection: I work on theory of precision atomic structure and have collaborated with the Lund attosecond group of 2023 laureate L'Huillier; no direct collaboration with Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp is apparent from my profile.
